purpose: Independent practice of A10.1 — measuring with non-standard units. Used as Lesson 4 consolidation artifact.
student_learning_goal: I can measure with cubes, hands, or footsteps.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can measure with cubes, hands, or footsteps.
header.character_watermark: Max the Measure Moose in the top-right corner of the header, holding linking cubes. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Each picture shows an object with cubes lined up beside it. Count the cubes. Write the number.
parts.visual_layout: Four object-and-cubes rows stacked vertically. Each row shows an object on the left with a row of small cubes lined up beneath/beside it: (1) pencil + 5 cubes, (2) crayon + 3 cubes, (3) book + 7 cubes, (4) eraser + 2 cubes. Beside each row, a label line ' = ___ cubes long'.

image_placeholders.description: Four measurement rows in B&W line art for a Kindergarten worksheet. Each row shows an object aligned with linking cubes: Row 1: a pencil with exactly 5 small cubes lined up tightly beneath it (no gaps). Row 2: a crayon with 3 cubes. Row 3: a book with 7 cubes. Row 4: an eraser with 2 cubes. Each row ~3in × 1in. Beside each row, a label line ' = ___ cubes long' with an empty number box.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P1_CUBES at Part 1: instructions ask the child to count cubes. Keywords name the visual unit (cubes) and example objects (pencil, book) that have cubes lined up beside them.

parts.answer_key: Pencil = 5 cubes. Crayon = 3 cubes. Book = 7 cubes. Eraser = 2 cubes.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each object. Draw a line from the object to the BEST unit to measure it.
parts.visual_layout: Two-column matching activity. Left column has 4 objects stacked vertically: pencil (small), book (small), table (medium), classroom (large). Right column has 3 unit options stacked: cubes, hand-spans, footsteps. Generous gap between columns for line-drawing.

image_placeholders.description: A two-column matching layout for a Kindergarten worksheet, B&W line art. Left column shows 4 objects stacked vertically: pencil (~1in tall), book (~1.5in tall), classroom desk (~2in tall), full classroom outline (~2.5in tall). Right column shows 3 unit options stacked: a small cube icon labelled 'cubes', a hand-span icon labelled 'hand-spans', a footprint icon labelled 'footsteps'. Wide gap between columns for line-drawing.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P2_MATCH at Part 2: instructions ask the child to match objects to the best measurement unit. Keywords name the three unit options shown in the right column.

parts.answer_key: Pencil → cubes. Book → cubes (or hand-spans). Desk → hand-spans. Classroom → footsteps. Accept reasonable matches; the sense is: small=cubes, medium=hands, large=footsteps.

parts.student_instructions: Pick 3 things at home. Measure each with cubes (or any same-size objects you have, like Legos!). Draw and write the count.
parts.visual_layout: Three response rows stacked vertically. Each row has a left column with a blank drawing box (~2.5in × 1.5in) and a right column with a label line ' = ___ cubes long'.

image_placeholders.description: Three measurement rows in B&W line art for a Kindergarten worksheet. Each row has a blank drawing box on the left (~2.5in × 1.5in, thin border) and a label line on the right reading ' = ___ cubes long' with an empty number box. Designed for the child to draw home objects and record cube counts.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P3_TABLE at Part 3: instructions ask the child to measure 3 home objects with cubes. Keywords name the activity (measure) and location (home).

parts.answer_key: Any 3 home objects with reasonable cube counts. Common: spoon ≈ 4 cubes, book ≈ 8 cubes, shoe ≈ 5 cubes.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, count how many footsteps from your bed to your kitchen. Write the number.
teacher_notes: Lesson 4 consolidation artifact. Use Part 1 as the formative signal for the gap-counting trap — children who get the count wrong even with images showing tightly-aligned cubes need the 'no gaps' re-loop.
